@graph.name: Nikita Boyarkin
@graph.description: Data / product analyst with a working portfolio of experiments, SQL pipelines and retention analyses, each written up as a public case study. Flagship: Volta Neobank — a KYC A/B at +5.72 pp conversion and EUR 208.5K modelled A/B impact over 12 months on synthetic data, plus EUR 282K retention LTV across 23 linked sub-cases.

item.name: A/B Testing Methodology Toolkit
item.description: CUPED cuts variance 17.7% (SE 0.00360 → 0.00327) and the delta method finds a +0.51 pp CTR lift at p < 0.0001 with SRM p = 0.8376 — all 18 modules calibrated by simulation

item.name: Browser Mini-Games — Analytics Arcade
item.description: 10 games: 7 analytics and 3 arcade, one file with no server; Playwright smoke tests catch load failures

item.name: Causal / Uplift — CUPED and Individual Treatment Effects
item.description: CUPED cuts the standard error 26% (5.5k users per arm instead of 10k), and a pre-registered break-even threshold of 0.05 ships the campaign to new users only.

item.name: CRM Experiment Lab — Segment-Stage Randomization, GCG and Net Effect
item.description: Segment-stage randomization holds SRM at p=0.266, GCG uplift is +0.9968 [0.9433, 1.0502], and the net effect is +50.5 per 1,000 treated — positive, but the unsubscribe guardrail breaches.

item.name: Data Analyst Telegram Bot
item.description: From a CSV — p-value, lift and 95% CI in under 30 seconds, plus a power note and a chart; /export returns a standalone HTML report

item.name: Volta Neobank — Product Analytics
item.description: KYC fix: +5.72pp conversion (p<0.0001) → €208.5K over 12 months at 13.9× ROI; M3 retention +9.2pp

item.name: Churn Prediction — Leakage-Free Retention Model
item.description: The top 10% riskiest catches 54.4% of churners at 5.44x lift, but only 1.75x on the at-risk subgroup: 69.7% of the cohort is a near-guaranteed negative by construction.

item.name: Cohort Analysis Dashboard
item.description: Python inside Tableau: 4 cohort calculations on a TabPy server and 65 tests; the cohort matrix replaces average retention and shows churn speed and where monetization diverges

item.name: Delivery Control Tower
item.description: Best WAPE 6.01% at h=7 with seasonal_naive; delivery time barely moves with load (rho = −0.092), yet snacks take 40.0 min against 26.6 min for pizza; the mp channel share grew 5.7 pp

item.name: GMV Drop RCA — root cause on real data
item.description: UK decile-1 explains 56.2% of the named drop (−£195,218.25); the full attribution reconciles to £0.00 against an overall −10.0% decline

item.name: LinkedIn Content Analytics
item.description: 50,101 impressions, 9,440 reach, 1.71% ER over 12.10.2025 — 11.10.2026; three of four comparisons landed inside the noise, and that is recorded as the result

item.name: ML Fundamentals — scikit-learn Pipeline
item.description: A split reproducible without a seed (Train (8, 5), Test (2, 5)), four synthetic datasets and 21 tests (7 + 9 + 5) that keep the pipeline runnable

item.name: Product A/B & Funnel Analytics — Conversion versus Retention
item.description: SHIP: activation → paid +19.59% (p=0.000946) with no guardrail degradation; at an equal step conversion adds +10.00% to LTV versus +8.65% for retention

item.name: Promo Margin Lab — what a promo rouble actually earns
item.description: Promo returns +68.5 m RUB of revenue and −24.4 m RUB of profit; 97.9% of waves lose money at a breakeven depth of 1.0–19.5% against 25.4% actual, and on one budget the optimiser earns +231 496 ₽ versus +136 648 ₽ for top-15%

item.name: Python Analytics Playground
item.description: pytest coverage ≥80%; modules stay small and single-purpose, requirements live in the PRD, and the tool extends without breakage

item.name: RAG Evaluation Harness — retrieval and generation metrics
item.description: recall@5 and MRR = 1.00 over 20 questions and 0.00 on an 11-question control set of retrieval misses (MRR@all 0.12) — the metric can fall; correctness 0.37 for the offline baseline (faithfulness ≡1.00 is an extractive invariant); retrieval and generation scored separately

item.name: RFM Analysis of Bank Clients
item.description: Six named segments; the top 20% of clients hold 38.2% of revenue (Gini 0.324), and Champions — 6.4% of the base — drive 12.1% of revenue

item.name: Sales Calls Analytics Dashboard
item.description: An answer in a minute: which step loses the client and what to fix; the funnel yields weighted contact loss and a first A/B scenario

item.name: SERP Rank Lab
item.description: On a synthetic log: +34.45% revenue per search for −16.84% CTR; the rollout returns −14.26% (p = 0.11) and −16.05% conversion → do not ship

item.name: SQL Analytics Case Study
item.description: The funnel drops 78% at add-to-cart → checkout (54% is the view→cart step); retention falls from ~19.5% (D1) to ~4% (D30); only 3.5% repeat; on real data 72.4% return

item.name: Classifieds liquidity — a measurability audit
item.description: The proxy reads 0.2413 against a truth of 0.3070, an error of −0.0657 (−21.4%); after correction the worst category misses by 1.61 pp, and paid visibility yields −2.47% contacts per session at p = 0.308

item.name: Product Analytics + A/B on Supabase
item.description: A/B concluded on a seeded stream: control 29.6% vs treatment 40.7%, +11.1pp at p ≈ 1.7e-10 (chi-square); metrics computed in the live DB for any client

item.name: Product Analytics Dashboard (Streamlit)
item.description: Funnel, Retention, Revenue, and Segments read from one consistent base; the same UI became the Supabase project's presentation layer

item.name: TaskFlow — PostHog Product Analytics Pipeline
item.description: Onboarding test on a seeded stream: completion 55.9% → 70.8% (+26.6%, χ² = 40.10, p < 0.0001, SRM p = 0.90), and 6.3% of completed signups reach a paid upgrade

item.name: Airflow DAG Platform
item.description: Three DAGs on one shared template and 72 tests without Airflow services or a DB; the full DAG runs in 440 s, 413 s of it in the forecast task

item.name: ClickHouse — ten SQL cases on 50M rows
item.description: The snapshot and seven DuckDB twins agree, slow and fast SQL are pinned as identical by a test, and the projection clears the ≥10× speed-up threshold the suite asserts on a full scan

item.name: Digital Garden — EQ in IT
item.description: Links over chronology: backlinks make each note a node, and the graph turns note accumulation into a navigable structure

item.name: OSS catalog — 47 projects from one source
item.description: 47 project pages and 15 metadata fields are built from one TOML file; a repeated render is idempotent, and 26 tests cover all three record-matching branches

item.name: Scrolly English Speaking
item.description: Narrative and visualization in sync: the chart changes as the reader reaches a paragraph; a new scene is just a data file plus MDX

item.name: This Portfolio Site
item.description: Invalid frontmatter breaks the build, not the deploy; no link hardcodes the base; adding a project needs no code changes

item.name: Matemarketing 2026 Programme — a static replica
item.description: The grid matches the original to the pixel: 99 px time column, 420 px hall column, 391 px card, 550 px row, grid top at y = 414; tests catch data and layout drift

item.name: Volta — Funnel Analysis
item.description: KYC — 56.6% step conversion; registration — 2,682 users; 1,269 of 10,000 reach the first transaction

item.name: Volta — KYC Progress-Bar A/B Test
item.description: KYC conversion 55.8% → 61.5%: +5.72pp at p<0.0001, above the MDE; gate passed, +€208.5K over 12 months

item.name: Volta — Retention & Cohorts
item.description: Post-fix cohorts hold 61–67% at M1 vs 51–53% pre-fix; M3 +9.2pp, Premium LTV 2.7× Free, +€282K/yr

item.name: Volta — User Segmentation
item.description: K=4 (Power 12% / Growth 24% / Casual 32% / Dormant 32%); Power drive 41% of revenue, 68% → 92%; migration +€310K/yr

item.name: Volta — Churn Prediction
item.description: Random Forest adds +0.03 ROC-AUC over LR; top driver is device-error rate 23.7%, usage_frequency 18.7% and days_since_last_activity 16.5%

item.name: Volta — RFM Analysis
item.description: Champions — 23.9% of the base with all three axes high (91/93/93); At Risk 11.5% and Lost 23.2% are a large reactivation reserve

item.name: Volta — CLV Modeling
item.description: Power > Growth > Casual > Dormant holds across all three methods; Gamma-Gamma Power €5,166 vs Dormant €27.7 — a ~187× gap

item.name: Volta — Marketing Attribution
item.description: Referral leads in all four models (€218–264K); Shapley takes referral to €263.7K and drops display to €125.0K

item.name: Volta — Anomaly Detection
item.description: Isolation Forest — best F1 (50.4%, 401 detections); Z-score — precision 80.5% at recall 24.7% (123 detections)

item.name: Volta — Spend Analysis
item.description: Bills (25.8%) and travel (20.2%) — nearly half the turnover; groceries most frequent (18,238 transactions, €45.8 ticket)

item.name: Volta — Support & Churn
item.description: Churn rises with ticket count: 37.1% (0) → 81.1% (3+); users with 3+ tickets churn 2.2× more; CSAT bands barely discriminate (52–55%)

item.name: Volta — NPS Trends
item.description: NPS hovers near zero: peak +12.9 (2024-10), bottom −1.8 (2024-09); fees −59.4 is the main negative, app_quality +30.3

item.name: Volta — JTBD × Cohorts
item.description: JTBD segment × cohort are NOT independent (p<0.001); Dormant 39.4% among Digital Newcomers 45+ vs 15.1% among Family Budgeters

item.name: Volta — Traveler Unit Economics
item.description: Net margin −€0.45 per €100 FX; break-even needs FX cost cut 1.00% → 0.55%

item.name: Volta — Premium Upsell
item.description: Premium Status 41.2%, anchor 17.3% vs Digital Newcomers 45+ 1.8% (z=34, p<0.001)

item.name: Volta — Referral Segments
item.description: Anchor 29.6% vs 45+ 4.8% and families 8.6%; the gap opens at accept (78% vs 26% vs 40%), in-app 20.6% vs link 14.3%

item.name: Volta — Assisted CAC vs LTV
item.description: The anchor clears the ≥3 gate only via referral at LTV/CAC 3.62; 45+ clears none: assisted 0.41; blended 0.66; 50-month payback

item.name: Volta — FX Sourcing Feasibility
item.description: The 0.55% gate needs ≈ €332M/month at SOM scale; today's ~€2.7M/mo is ~122× lower; ~0.20pp per order of magnitude; Interbank Prime 0.745%

item.name: Volta — Segment Premium Offers
item.description: 45+ 1.6%→5.0%, families 4.4%→8.6%, travelers 8.8%→12.6%; anchor +0.86pp — the gap is not closed

item.name: Volta — Anchor Launch CAC at Scale
item.description: LTV/CAC ≥3 holds only to ~70K users (31% of SOM); at SOM 225K it is 1.76× with a 17.0-month payback

item.name: Volta — Dormant 45+ Win-back
item.description: human +5.34pp, light-touch +2.77pp; light-touch pays off at 30–60d (ROI 2.54) and 60–90d (1.26), human overall 0.40

item.name: Volta — Causal Validation of KYC (DiD)
item.description: M3 retention: DiD ATT +9.09pp (95% CI [+6.21, +11.96]); activation naive +6.29pp vs DiD +4.92pp
